title: Build the Life You Want
author: Arthur C. Brooks and Oprah Winfrey
blurb: Arthur Brooks and Oprah Winfrey argue that happiness is not a destination or a passing feeling. It is a direction you can move in, a little at a time. They break happiness into three macronutrients: enjoyment, satisfaction, and purpose. They point out that unhappiness will never fully disappear, and it can even be useful. The first half of the book teaches emotional self-management. You learn to observe your feelings instead of being ruled by them, to choose emotions like gratitude, hope, compassion, and humor, and to spend less time focused on yourself. The second half shows where to invest the energy that frees up. The authors name four pillars: family, friendship, meaningful work, and faith or transcendence. They close by urging readers to share what they learn, because teaching happiness helps make it stick.

lessons.t: Happier Is the Goal, Not Happy
lessons.b: Happiness is a direction you move toward through daily choices, not a final destination you arrive at and keep forever.
A happy life needs a balanced diet of enjoyment, satisfaction, and purpose, and satisfaction grows when you manage your wants rather than endlessly piling up more.

lessons.t: Step Back and Watch Your Feelings
lessons.b: Metacognition means noticing your emotions as signals rather than commands, which lets you respond thoughtfully instead of reacting on autopilot.
